analysis: This batch is documentation only. It adds changelog.d/ssd-eviction-selection.md (head lines 1-10) and changes docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md: the date at base/head line 3 and a new paragraph at head lines 531-546. Both describe a change to SSD LRU eviction victim selection. The store tries one linear SSDBlockIndex.oldest probe first. If that file is busy or cannot be unlinked, it falls back to an oldestFirstSnapshot heap. The docs say the following controls are retained: file leases, epoch validation, the removal lock, bounded attempts, and returning control to the disk budget after external-loss reconciliation. Relevant threat: T-041, whose LRU disk budget, TTL and at-rest exposure are bounded by eviction. The described behavior keeps the same oldest-by-last-hit order for stable inputs, so the at-rest exposure window and disk-budget mitigation are unchanged as documented. The doc admits that concurrent schedules may pick different victims, which affects which file is evicted, not retention bounds. No source for provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.swift or SSDBlockIndex.swift was supplied, so these claims are unverified. The next pass needs that source to confirm: (1) the snapshot pass is truly bounded and terminates, with no unbounded loop or CPU DoS under repeated busy files; (2) busy or leased files are never deleted while a read or adoption is in flight, preserving staging-reservation release; (3) the disk budget is rechecked after reconciliation, so a failure cannot leave the budget permanently exceeded (T-016/T-041 availability and at-rest size); (4) eviction still does not rotate the cache epoch, per the T-041 detection_hint. No regression is identifiable from the docs themselves.
